headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress make gpt-engineer dangerous alongside Botpress, with prompt-injection and leakage risks from default file-based workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while gpt-engineer reads and writes project files and can ingest generated content through its file-based workflow. A shared workspace creates a plausible instruction-hijack path even without explicit MCP or clipboard bridging. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so uncertainty is moderate.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into a shared project directory that gpt-engineer reads
IF gpt-engineer treats file contents as instructions during generation
mitigations: Keep Botpress and gpt-engineer in separate directories
Require manual review of any Botpress-generated text before reuse
Prefix imported Botpress content with a non-executable delimiter
Disable automatic ingestion of support transcripts into coding prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress and handles files in a user-specified project directory, while Botpress is documented only as a support agent with no stated data-minimization or local-only guarantee. If support content or secrets enter the shared workspace, gpt-engineer can transmit them to a configured model backend. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Botpress stores customer transcripts or secrets in the same project directory
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents to its configured model backend
mitigations: Do not place support transcripts in the coding workspace
Redact secrets before any file handoff
Use a separate least-privilege account for gpt-engineer
Restrict outbound network destinations where possible
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists for uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and gpt-engineer can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Even though gpt-engineer does not modify git state, both agents can mutate the same project directory and dependency environment, creating racey overwrite and environment-drift conflicts in default multi-instance use. The shared-state risk is explicit in gpt-engineer's concurrency model.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF Botpress installs or changes packages while gpt-engineer is writing files or running subprocesses
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate project directory
Serialize package installation steps
Snapshot the workspace before either agent writes
Use a lock file around dependency changes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support-facing text, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run them, so Botpress output could become upstream input for code generation or execution without a verification gate. That creates a plausible cascade from conversational content into actionable code or commands. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF Botpress output is pasted into gpt-engineer prompts or files
IF gpt-engineer proceeds from generated text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before any generated code is run
Separate support text from code-generation prompts
Add a checklist to verify facts before execution
Limit gpt-engineer to draft-only mode for imported content
requires-engineering: add automated validation before run prompts

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a support agent with no documented residency or retention controls, while gpt-engineer explicitly handles generated source code and the OPENAI_API_KEY. The profiles do not show a concrete regulatory mismatch such as PHI or EU PII, so compliance risk is limited to documented-policy gaps rather than a clear breach. Because the relevant compliance fields are sparse, uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Botpress and then copied into gpt-engineer
IF the operator requires retention or residency guarantees that are not documented
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Document retention and deletion expectations before use
Keep API keys out of shared project files
Review vendor data-processing terms
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
